1.solution:
For \(P = \dfrac{x^{3}y}{z^{2}}\), the fractional errors add with the powers as coefficients:
\[\frac{\Delta P}{P} = 3\frac{\Delta x}{x} + \frac{\Delta y}{y} + 2\frac{\Delta z}{z}.\]
Substituting the percentage errors:
\[\frac{\Delta P}{P}\,(\%) = (3 \times 0.6) + 3 + (2 \times 1.3) = 1.8 + 3 + 2.6 = 7.4\%.\]

2.solution:
Work done in moving a charge between two points equals charge times potential difference:
\[W = q\left(V_{B} - V_{A}\right) = q\big(V - (-5)\big) = q(V + 5).\]
Solving for \(V\):
\[\frac{W}{q} = V + 5 \quad\Rightarrow\quad V = \frac{W}{q} - 5.\]

3.subtopic: Circular Motion — Angular Velocity, Centripetal Force, Vertical Circle
3.solution:
Let \(v_{2}\) be the speed at the top and \(v_{1}\) at the bottom. By energy conservation \(v_{1}^{2} = v_{2}^{2} + 4gL\).
Maximum (bottom) and minimum (top) tensions:
\[T_{\max} = \frac{mv_{1}^{2}}{L} + mg, \qquad T_{\min} = \frac{mv_{2}^{2}}{L} - mg.\]
Therefore
\[\frac{T_{\max}}{T_{\min}} = \frac{v_{1}^{2} + gL}{v_{2}^{2} - gL} = \frac{v_{2}^{2} + 5gL}{v_{2}^{2} - gL} = 3.\]
Solving: \(3v_{2}^{2} - 3gL = v_{2}^{2} + 5gL \Rightarrow 2v_{2}^{2} = 8gL \Rightarrow v_{2}^{2} = 4gL\), so \(v_{2} = 2\sqrt{gL}\) (i.e. \(v^{2} = 4gL\)).

4.solution:
For a shunt, the galvanometer current is \(I_{g} = \dfrac{5}{100}I\). The shunt resistance is
\[S = \frac{G}{\left(\dfrac{I}{I_{g}} - 1\right)} = \frac{G}{\dfrac{100}{5} - 1} = \frac{G}{19}.\]
4.note: Source printed options as (a)(b)(c)(c); 4th relabelled D = G/21.

6.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
6.solution:
Point P is equidistant from both wires and the lines PA, PB are mutually perpendicular, so each wire is at distance \(X\) with \(2X^{2} = 5^{2}\), giving \(X = \dfrac{5}{\sqrt{2}}\) cm. The fields \(B_{1}, B_{2}\) are perpendicular, so
\[B_{net} = \frac{\mu_{0}}{2\pi X}\sqrt{I_{1}^{2} + I_{2}^{2}} = \frac{4\pi \times 10^{-7}}{2\pi \times \frac{5}{\sqrt{2}} \times 10^{-2}}\sqrt{4^{2} + 3^{2}}.\]
\[= \big(2 \times 10^{-7} \times 20\sqrt{2}\big) \times 5 = 2\sqrt{2} \times 10^{-5}\ \text{T}.\]

7.subtopic: Radiation — Stefan, Wien, Newton's Law of Cooling, Black Body
7.solution:
By Stefan's law for a sphere, \(P = \sigma A T^{4} = \sigma (4\pi R^{2}) T^{4}\), so \(P \propto R^{2}T^{4}\).
With \(R \to 2R\) and \(T \to 2T\):
\[\frac{P'}{P} = \frac{(2R)^{2}(2T)^{4}}{R^{2}T^{4}} = 4 \times 16 = 64.\]
Thus \(P' = 64P\).

8.subtopic: Power in AC Circuit — Average, Factor, Wattless
8.solution:
Net reactance \(|X_{L} - X_{C}| = |70 - 130| = 60\ \Omega\).
Impedance \(Z = \sqrt{R^{2} + (X_{L} - X_{C})^{2}} = \sqrt{80^{2} + 60^{2}} = 100\ \Omega\).
Power factor \(\cos\phi = \dfrac{R}{Z} = \dfrac{80}{100} = 0.8\).

9.solution:
Stationary lift: \(T = 2\pi\sqrt{\dfrac{l}{g}} = \sqrt{3}\ \text{s}\).
Lift accelerating up with \(g/3\): effective gravity \(g' = g + \dfrac{g}{3} = \dfrac{4g}{3}\).
\[\frac{T'}{T} = \sqrt{\frac{g}{g'}} = \sqrt{\frac{3}{4}} = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}.\]
\[T' = \frac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\times\sqrt{3} = \frac{3}{2} = 1.5\ \text{s}.\]

10.subtopic: Self-Inductance, Energy Stored, and LR Circuit
10.solution:
Three equal inductors in series give \(L_{eq} = L + L + L = 3L\).
Energy stored \(U = \dfrac{1}{2}L_{eq}I^{2} = \dfrac{1}{2}(3L)I^{2} = \dfrac{3}{2}LI^{2}\).

11.solution:
First member of Balmer (\(n_{1}=2, n_{2}=3\)): \(\dfrac{1}{\lambda_{1}} = R\left(\dfrac{1}{4} - \dfrac{1}{9}\right) = \dfrac{5R}{36}\).
First member of Paschen (\(n_{1}=3, n_{2}=4\)): \(\dfrac{1}{\lambda_{2}} = R\left(\dfrac{1}{9} - \dfrac{1}{16}\right) = \dfrac{7R}{144}\).
Since \(f = \dfrac{c}{\lambda}\), \(\dfrac{f_{1}}{f_{2}} = \dfrac{\lambda_{2}}{\lambda_{1}} = \dfrac{5R/36}{7R/144} = \dfrac{5 \times 144}{36 \times 7} = \dfrac{20}{7}\).

12.chapter: Magnetic Fields Due to Electric Current
12.subtopic: Magnetic Moment of Current Loop and Galvanometer Instruments
12.solution:
For an orbiting electron, the orbital magnetic moment is \(m_{orb} = \dfrac{e}{2m}L\) (the gyromagnetic relation).
Hence the ratio of angular momentum to magnetic moment is
\[\frac{L}{m_{orb}} = \frac{2m}{e}.\]

13.subtopic: Isothermal, Adiabatic, Isobaric, and Isochoric Processes
13.solution:
All three start with equal pressure-state and reach the SAME final pressure after doubling volume; work back from equal final pressures.
Isothermal (X): \(P_{i}V = P_{f}(2V) \Rightarrow P_{i,X} = 2P_{f}\).
Adiabatic (Y): \(P_{i}V^{\gamma} = P_{f}(2V)^{\gamma} \Rightarrow P_{i,Y} = P_{f}(2)^{3/2} = 2\sqrt{2}\,P_{f}\).
Isobaric (Z): pressure unchanged, \(P_{i,Z} = P_{f}\).
Ratio of initial pressures \(X:Y:Z = 2 : 2\sqrt{2} : 1\).

14.subtopic: Self-Inductance, Energy Stored, and LR Circuit
14.solution: Energy stored in an inductor is \(W = \dfrac{1}{2}LI^{2}\). With unit current \(I = 1\ \text{A}\), \(W = \dfrac{1}{2}L\), i.e. \(L = 2W\). So self-inductance is numerically twice the work done in establishing the flux for unit current.

15.subtopic: Doppler Effect — Moving Source and Observer
15.solution: For a source approaching a stationary observer, \(n' = n\left(\dfrac{v}{v - v_{s}}\right) > n\), so the apparent frequency increases. Since \(v\) (speed of sound in the medium) is unchanged and \(\lambda' = v/n'\), the apparent wavelength decreases.

16.subtopic: Surface Tension, Surface Energy, and Capillary Rise
16.solution:
Capillary rise \(h \propto \dfrac{1}{r}\), so \(h_{P}r_{P} = h_{Q}r_{Q}\). Diameter of Q is 80% of P, so \(r_{Q} = 0.8\,r_{P}\).
\[h_{Q} = \frac{h_{P}r_{P}}{r_{Q}} = \frac{2.4 \times r_{P}}{0.8\,r_{P}} = 3\ \text{cm}.\]

17.solution:
Fourth overtone of a closed pipe is the 9th harmonic: \(f_{c} = \dfrac{9v}{4l_{c}}\).
Fifth overtone of an open pipe is the 6th harmonic: \(f_{o} = \dfrac{6v}{2l_{o}} = \dfrac{3v}{l_{o}}\).
Setting \(f_{c} = f_{o}\):
\[\frac{9v}{4l_{c}} = \frac{3v}{l_{o}} \Rightarrow \frac{l_{c}}{l_{o}} = \frac{9}{12} = \frac{3}{4}.\]

18.solution:
With a slab of thickness \(t\) and dielectric constant \(k=3\), \(C' = \dfrac{A\varepsilon_{0}}{d - t + \frac{t}{k}}\). Required \(C' = 1.5\,C = \dfrac{3}{2}\dfrac{A\varepsilon_{0}}{d}\).
\[d - t + \frac{t}{3} = \frac{2d}{3} \Rightarrow d - \frac{2t}{3} = \frac{2d}{3} \Rightarrow \frac{2t}{3} = \frac{d}{3} \Rightarrow t = \frac{d}{2}.\]

19.subtopic: Satellites, Orbital Motion, and Kepler's Laws
19.solution:
Two masses orbit their common centre on a circle of radius \(r\); their separation is \(2r\). The gravitational attraction provides the centripetal force:
\[\frac{Gm^{2}}{(2r)^{2}} = \frac{mv^{2}}{r} \Rightarrow v^{2} = \frac{Gm}{4r} \Rightarrow v = \sqrt{\frac{Gm}{4r}}.\]

20.subtopic: Moment of Inertia, Theorems, and Radius of Gyration
20.solution:
Each mass is at distance \(\dfrac{L}{\sqrt{2}}\) (half the diagonal) from the centre. The moment of inertia about the central perpendicular axis is
\[I = 4M\left(\frac{L}{\sqrt{2}}\right)^{2} = 4M\cdot\frac{L^{2}}{2} = 2ML^{2}.\]
Radius of gyration \(k = \sqrt{\dfrac{I}{4M}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{2ML^{2}}{4M}} = \dfrac{L}{\sqrt{2}}.\)

21.subtopic: p-n Junction Diode — Biasing, I-V, and Rectifiers
21.solution: In a reverse-biased p-n junction the depletion layer widens and the potential barrier increases. The electric field is concentrated across the depletion region and is maximum there.

22.solution:
The difference in lengths is \((l_{2} - l_{1}) + (l_{2}\alpha_{2} - l_{1}\alpha_{1})\Delta t\). For this to be independent of temperature, the coefficient of \(\Delta t\) must vanish:
\[l_{2}\alpha_{2} = l_{1}\alpha_{1} \Rightarrow \frac{l_{1}}{l_{2}} = \frac{\alpha_{2}}{\alpha_{1}}.\]

23.solution:
For two coplanar concentric loops with \(R_{1} > R_{2}\), the field of the larger loop is taken uniform over the smaller, so
\[M = \frac{\mu_{0}\pi R_{2}^{2}}{2R_{1}} \Rightarrow M \propto \frac{R_{2}^{2}}{R_{1}}.\]

24.solution:
At the highest point the spring is unstretched, so the amplitude equals the static extension: \(kx = mg \Rightarrow \dfrac{m}{k} = \dfrac{x}{g}\).
\[T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{m}{k}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{x}{g}} = 0.1\ \text{s} \Rightarrow x = \frac{g}{4\pi^{2}}(0.1)^{2}\cdot\frac{1}{1} = \frac{10}{400\pi^{2}} = \frac{1}{40\pi^{2}}\ \text{m}.\]
Maximum speed \(v_{\max} = x\omega = x\cdot\dfrac{2\pi}{T} = \dfrac{1}{40\pi^{2}}\cdot\dfrac{2\pi}{0.1} = \dfrac{1}{40\pi^{2}}\cdot 20\pi = \dfrac{1}{2\pi}\ \text{m/s}.\)

25.subtopic: Prism — Deviation, Dispersion, and Refractive Index
25.solution:
For a thin prism \(\delta = (\mu - 1)A\). In air \(\mu_{1} = \dfrac{3}{2}\). In water the relative index is \(\mu_{2} = \dfrac{{}_{a}\mu_{g}}{{}_{a}\mu_{w}} = \dfrac{3/2}{4/3} = \dfrac{9}{8}\).
\[\frac{\delta_{2}}{\delta_{1}} = \frac{\mu_{2} - 1}{\mu_{1} - 1} = \frac{9/8 - 1}{3/2 - 1} = \frac{1/8}{1/2} = \frac{1}{4}.\]
So \(\delta_{2}:\delta_{1} = 1:4\).

26.subtopic: Transistors — BJT, CE Amplifier, and Gain
26.solution:
Here \(\alpha = \dfrac{I_{C}}{I_{E}} = 0.95\). The CE current gain is
\[\beta = \frac{\alpha}{1 - \alpha} = \frac{0.95}{0.05} = 19.\]

27.solution:
Three segments: \(l = \dfrac{3\lambda}{2} \Rightarrow \lambda = \dfrac{2(0.9)}{3} = 0.6\ \text{m}\).
Wave speed \(v = \sqrt{\dfrac{T}{m}} = \sqrt{\dfrac{40}{0.1}} = 20\ \text{m/s}\); frequency \(n = \dfrac{v}{\lambda} = \dfrac{20}{0.6} = \dfrac{100}{3}\ \text{Hz}\).
Maximum particle velocity \(= a\,\omega = a(2\pi n) = (0.3 \times 10^{-2})(2\pi)\dfrac{100}{3} = \dfrac{\pi}{5}\ \text{m/s}.\)

28.solution:
Figure shows a rod pivoted at one end, released from the vertical-up position; at angle \(\theta\) from vertical the weight \(mg\) acts at the centre \(L/2\). Torque about pivot \(\tau = mg\sin\theta\cdot\dfrac{L}{2}\).
With \(I = \dfrac{mL^{2}}{3}\):
\[\frac{mL^{2}}{3}\alpha = mg\sin\theta\frac{L}{2} \Rightarrow \alpha = \frac{3g\sin\theta}{2L}.\]

29.subtopic: Average KE, Equipartition, and Specific Heats
29.solution:
From Mayer's relation \(C_{p} - C_{v} = R\). Dividing by \(C_{p}\): \(1 - \dfrac{1}{\gamma} = \dfrac{R}{C_{p}}\), so
\[C_{p} = \frac{R\gamma}{\gamma - 1}.\]

30.solution:
From the figure, \(q_{1} = +6q\) at the origin and \(q_{2} = -3q\) at distance \(L\); the proton lies on the x-axis beyond \(q_{2}\). Let \(a\) be the distance of the proton from \(q_{2}\), so its distance from \(q_{1}\) is \(L + a\). For equilibrium the net field is zero:
\[\frac{6q}{(L+a)^{2}} = \frac{3q}{a^{2}} \Rightarrow \frac{2}{(L+a)^{2}} = \frac{1}{a^{2}} \Rightarrow \sqrt{2}\,a = L + a.\]
\[a = \frac{L}{\sqrt{2} - 1}.\]
Distance from \(q_{1}\): \(L + a = L + \dfrac{L}{\sqrt{2}-1} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}\,L}{\sqrt{2} - 1} = \left(\dfrac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{2}-1}\right)L.\)

31.subtopic: Circular Motion — Angular Velocity, Centripetal Force, Vertical Circle
31.solution:
Using \(\omega^{2} = \omega_{0}^{2} - 2\alpha\theta\). After 24 rotations \(\omega = \dfrac{\omega_{0}}{3}\):
\[\frac{\omega_{0}^{2}}{9} = \omega_{0}^{2} - 2\alpha(2\pi\cdot 24) \Rightarrow 2\alpha(48\pi) = \frac{8\omega_{0}^{2}}{9}.\]
Total rotations to rest: \(0 = \omega_{0}^{2} - 2\alpha(2\pi n') \Rightarrow n' = \dfrac{\omega_{0}^{2}}{4\alpha\pi}\). Substituting \(\alpha\) gives \(n' = 27\). Additional rotations \(= 27 - 24 = 3\).

32.subtopic: Young's Double Slit, Biprism, and Interference
32.solution:
Since \(I \propto a^{2}\), the amplitude ratio is the square root of the intensity ratio:
\[\frac{a_{bright}}{a_{dark}} = \sqrt{\frac{I_{bright}}{I_{dark}}} = \sqrt{\frac{5}{1}} = \sqrt{5}:1.\]

33.subtopic: Surface Tension, Surface Energy, and Capillary Rise
33.solution:
The upward surface-tension force on the circular contact line is \(F = (2\pi r)T\), where \(2\pi r\) is the inner circumference. With \(F = 98\ \text{dyne} = 98 \times 10^{-5}\ \text{N}\) and \(T = 7\times 10^{-2}\ \text{N/m}\):
\[2\pi r = \frac{F}{T} = \frac{98 \times 10^{-5}}{7 \times 10^{-2}} = 14 \times 10^{-3}\ \text{m} = 1.4\ \text{cm}.\]

34.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
34.subtopic: Photoelectric Effect — Stopping Potential, Threshold, and Work Function
34.solution:
Einstein's equation: \(E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda} - \phi_{0}\) and \(2E = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_{1}} - \phi_{0}\).
Subtracting twice the first from the second: \(0 = \dfrac{hc}{\lambda_{1}} - \dfrac{2hc}{\lambda} + \phi_{0}\), i.e. \(\dfrac{1}{\lambda_{1}} = \dfrac{2}{\lambda} - \dfrac{\phi_{0}}{hc}\).
Since \(\dfrac{\phi_{0}}{hc} > 0\), \(\dfrac{1}{\lambda_{1}} < \dfrac{2}{\lambda}\), so \(\lambda_{1} > \dfrac{\lambda}{2}\) (and also \(\lambda_{1} < \lambda\) since energy increased). The valid choice is \(\lambda_{1} > \lambda/2\).

36.subtopic: Force on Current-Carrying Conductor and Parallel Wires
36.solution:
Force per unit length between parallel wires \(F \propto \dfrac{I_{1}I_{2}}{d}\). Currents doubled (\(I \to 2I\) each) and distance halved (\(d \to d/2\)):
\[\frac{F_{2}}{F} = \frac{(2I)(2I)}{I\cdot I}\cdot\frac{d}{d/2} = 4 \times 2 = 8 \Rightarrow F_{2} = 8F.\]

37.solution:
For a head-on elastic collision the coefficient of restitution \(e = 1\):
\[e = \frac{v_{2} - v_{1}}{u_{1} - u_{2}} = 1 \Rightarrow v_{2} - 4 = 5 - 3 = 2 \Rightarrow v_{2} = 6\ \text{m/s}.\]
The second particle moves at \(6\ \text{m/s}\) in the same direction.

38.subtopic: Isothermal, Adiabatic, Isobaric, and Isochoric Processes
38.solution: In an isothermal process temperature is constant, so \(\Delta U = 0\). By the first law \(Q = \Delta U + W = W\): all the heat supplied is converted into external work done by the gas.

39.subtopic: Reactance — Inductive, Capacitive, and Single-Element Circuits
39.solution:
From \(E = 100\sqrt{2}\sin(50t)\), \(E_{0} = 100\sqrt{2}\ \text{V}\), \(\omega = 50\ \text{rad/s}\).
Capacitive reactance \(X_{C} = \dfrac{1}{\omega C} = \dfrac{1}{50 \times 2\times10^{-6}} = 10^{4}\ \Omega\).
Peak current \(I_{0} = \dfrac{E_{0}}{X_{C}} = \dfrac{100\sqrt{2}}{10^{4}} = \sqrt{2}\times10^{-2}\ \text{A}\).
Ammeter reads RMS: \(I_{rms} = \dfrac{I_{0}}{\sqrt{2}} = 10^{-2}\ \text{A} = 10\ \text{mA}.\)

40.subtopic: Single Slit Diffraction and Resolving Power
40.solution:
Linear width of the central maximum \(\beta = \dfrac{2\lambda D}{d}\). Given \(\beta = 2d\):
\[2d = \frac{2\lambda D}{d} \Rightarrow D = \frac{d^{2}}{\lambda}.\]

41.subtopic: Surface Tension, Surface Energy, and Capillary Rise
41.solution:
Energy released on coalescence \(= T(n\cdot 4\pi r^{2} - 4\pi R^{2}) = 3E\), and the surface energy of the big drop is \(E = 4\pi R^{2}T\).
\[3(4\pi R^{2}T) = n(4\pi r^{2}T) - 4\pi R^{2}T \Rightarrow n\,r^{2} = 4R^{2} \Rightarrow n = \frac{4R^{2}}{r^{2}}.\]

\[\frac{\lambda_{Paschen}}{\lambda_{Balmer}} = \frac{9/R}{4/R} = \frac{9}{4}.\]

44.solution:
Potential energy of a dipole: \(U = -pE\cos\theta\). Initially aligned (\(\theta = 0\)): \(U_{1} = -pE\). After \(90^{\circ}\) rotation: \(U_{2} = -pE\cos90^{\circ} = 0\).
Work required \(= U_{2} - U_{1} = 0 - (-pE) = pE.\)

45.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
45.subtopic: Photoelectric Effect — Stopping Potential, Threshold, and Work Function
45.solution: Saturation photoelectric current is proportional to the intensity of incident light and independent of frequency (above threshold). Doubling the intensity doubles the saturation current.

46.solution:
The mass \(m\) hangs at R from two strings tied to fixed points P and Q with \(PQ = 2d\) and \(PR = QR = L\). Let O be the midpoint of PQ; then \(OR = \sqrt{L^{2} - d^{2}}\). When displaced slightly out of the plane, the mass swings about the line PQ as a pendulum of effective length \(OR\):
\[T = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{OR}{g}} = 2\pi\sqrt{\frac{(L^{2} - d^{2})^{1/2}}{g}}.\]

47.subtopic: RMS, Peak, and AC Source Characteristics
47.solution:
Current is maximum when \(\sin\left(50\pi t + \dfrac{\pi}{4}\right) = 1\), i.e. \(50\pi t + \dfrac{\pi}{4} = \dfrac{\pi}{2}\).
\[50\pi t = \frac{\pi}{4} \Rightarrow t = \frac{1}{200}\ \text{s}.\]

48.solution:
Fundamental of closed pipe (length \(L\)): \(n = \dfrac{v}{4L}\).
Second overtone of open pipe (length \(XL\)) is the 3rd harmonic: \(n' = \dfrac{3v}{2XL}\).
Setting \(n = n'\):
\[\frac{v}{4L} = \frac{3v}{2XL} \Rightarrow X = \frac{3 \times 4L}{2L} = 6.\]

49.subtopic: Transistors — BJT, CE Amplifier, and Gain
49.solution: By definition \(\alpha = \dfrac{I_{C}}{I_{E}} < 1\) (always less than unity) and \(\beta = \dfrac{\alpha}{1 - \alpha}\), which for \(\alpha\) close to 1 is large (\(> 1\)). Hence \(\beta > 1,\ \alpha < 1\).

50.solution:
Galvanometer resistance \(R_{g} = \dfrac{V_{g}}{I_{g}} = \dfrac{80\ \text{mV}}{16\ \text{mA}} = 5\ \Omega\).
To read up to 160 V a series resistance is added: \(V = I_{g}(R_{g} + R_{s})\).
\[R_{s} = \frac{V}{I_{g}} - R_{g} = \frac{160}{16\times10^{-3}} - 5 = 10000 - 5 = 9995\ \Omega\ \text{in series}.\]
